title: Velocity-Field Relationship Explorer
description: Log-log plot of drift velocity against electric field for electrons and holes in silicon, GaAs, and germanium, showing the linear regime, the transition, and velocity saturation. Overlays show the low-field tangent and the critical field, and an inset sketches the heating of the carrier energy distribution.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: semiconductor physics
drift velocity
velocity saturation
high-field transport
hot carriers

educational.topic: Drift velocity versus electric field and velocity saturation
learningObjectives: Identify the linear, transition, and saturated regimes of a velocity-field curve
Calculate drift velocity at a given field with the two-piece linear model
Explain why short-channel MOSFETs operate in velocity saturation

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders and selects with a real-time log-log plot and a probe readout
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe: students calculate with the two-piece model, then compare with the smooth model at the probe field
assessmentOpportunities: Estimate the critical field from the saturation velocity and mobility
Tabulate the error of the two-piece model at several fields
Place a MOSFET channel field on the curve and name the regime

controls.label: Show critical field marker
controls.purpose: Mark the saturation velocity and the critical (or peak) field

controls.label: Electric field
controls.purpose: Probe field for the readouts and the inset

equations: v = mu0 E / (1 + (E/Ec)^beta)^(1/beta), Ec = vsat/mu0, beta = 2 (electrons), 1 (holes)
GaAs electrons: v = (mu0 E + vsat (E/E0)^4)/(1 + (E/E0)^4), E0 = 4 kV/cm
Te = T + (2/3) q v E tauE / kB, tauE = 0.3 ps (inset only)
assumptions: Si: mu0 = 1400 and 450 cm^2/V.s, vsat = 1.07e7 and 8.4e6 cm/s at 300 K
GaAs: mu0 = 8500 and 400 cm^2/V.s, vsat about 8e6 and 1e7 cm/s
Ge: mu0 = 3900 and 1900 cm^2/V.s, vsat = 6e6 cm/s
Ge and GaAs holes use the same beta exponents as silicon
limitations: Temperature dependence is modeled for silicon only
The energy-distribution inset is a schematic heated Maxwellian
No velocity overshoot or impact ionization
